options.text: Scientists have a few tricks up

questions.solution:

• The error in the sentence lies in the phrase **"the universe other objects." **
 
• Here's a breakdown of the sentence:
 
• **"Scientists have a few tricks up"** - This fragment is grammatically correct and establishes the subject "Scientists" and their possession of "a few tricks."
 
• **"their sleeves for dealing with" **- This fragment is also grammatically correct. It indicates that the tricks are kept "up their sleeves" (a figurative expression meaning to keep something secret or hidden) and are used for "dealing with" various situations.
 
• **"No error" - **This option is incorrect because there is indeed an error in the sentence.
 
• **"the universe other objects" **- This fragment contains the error.** "the universe" **should be separated from **"other objects" **with the conjunction** "and" **to clearly indicate that the tricks are used for both the universe and other objects.

**Corrected sentence**__: *"Scientists have a few tricks up their sleeves for dealing with __**the universe and other objects**__."*

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

P. American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965

Q. the problems of collective action were popularized by the

R. that coercion or some other device must be present in order

S. for a group of individuals to act in their common interest
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **QPRS**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this arrangement, the sentence starts with the introduction of the problems of collective action being popularized. This provides the context for the subsequent parts.
 
 
• **Q. **"The problems of collective action were popularized by the"
 
• **P. **"American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965"
 
 
 
• These two parts go together as they establish who popularized the problems of collective action and when it happened. Mancur Olson, an American political economist, is mentioned as the individual responsible for bringing attention to these problems through his writing in 1965.
 
 
• **R.** "that coercion or some other device must be present in order"
 
• **S.** "for a group of individuals to act in their common interest"
 
 
 
• The last two parts connect to form a logical explanation. It states that in order for a group of individuals to act in their common interest, coercion or some other mechanism is necessary. This concludes the sentence by providing a solution or conclusion related to the problems of collective action.
 
• By following the order **QPRS**, the sentence maintains a logical flow by introducing the problem, establishing the authority, and providing an explanation or solution.

 

**Correct Arrangement**__: *The problems of collective action were popularized by the American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965 that coercion or some other device must be present in order for a group of individuals to act in their common interest.*

• The error in the sentence is with** subject-verb agreement.**
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"skull bones,"** which is plural.
 
• However, the verb **"has" **is in the singular form, which does not agree with the plural subject.
 
• To correct this error, the verb should be in the plural form **"have" **to match the subject "skull bones."

In this sentence, "general" indicates that the consensus is the opinion of the majority or a wide range of people.(उदाहरण के लिए, "आम सहमति यह थी कि नई नीति से सभी को लाभ होगा।" इस वाक्य में, "सामान्य" इंगित करता है कि सर्वसम्मति बहुमत या लोगों की एक विस्तृत श्रृंखला की राय है।)

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The lawyer said, "Your case is very complicated."

options.text: The lawyer said that my case was very complicated.
The lawyer reported that my case is very complicated.
The lawyer said that my case had been very complicated.
The lawyer warned that your case was very complicated.

questions.solution:
The correct sentence is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **indirect speech,** when reporting or narrating someone else's words, we typically shift the tense back one step into the past.
 
• Therefore, **the verb** **"is"** in the original direct speech changes to** "was" **in the indirect form to maintain the past tense.
 
• The **structure of indirect speech **in this case is: Reporting verb (said) + that + subject + past tense of the verb (was) + rest of the sentence.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *The lawyer said that my case was very complicated. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2,** "The lawyer reported that my case is very complicated," is not correct because it does not reflect the shift of tense required in indirect speech. It uses the present tense "is" instead of the past tense "was."
 
• **Option 3,** "The lawyer said that my case had been very complicated," is also not correct. It uses the past perfect tense ("had been") which is not necessary in this context, as the original sentence is already in the present tense.
 
• **Option 4**, "The lawyer warned that your case was very complicated," changes the meaning of the original sentence. It introduces the verb "warned" instead of "said," which alters the intention of the lawyer's statement.
